questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the web?
questions.explanation: Take each number in the outer ring as a 2 digit number and multiply them together. Write this answer plus 1 in the inner segment opposite.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the empty square?
questions.explanation: In each box, square the top numbers and subtract 4 to give the lower number.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the bottom circle?
questions.explanation: Starting from the left hand circle, working top to bottom in columns then to the next column to the right, add 1, then 2, then 3 etc. until the central circle, then subtract 11, 10, 9 etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the bottom grid?
questions.explanation: In each diagram, divide the top left value by 3, multiply it by the top right value, then multiply the answer by 4 to give the lower value.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Draw the correct number of circles in the blank square.
questions.correctAnswer: Four circles arranged at the top, right, bottom, and left of the square.
questions.explanation: Working in rows, using the left hand figure as a source, reflect around a vertical axis to give the middle figure, and reflect around a horizontal axis to give the right hand figure.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number comes next?
questions.explanation: The boxes follow the sequence of prime numbers multiplied by 5.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What goes in the empty box?
questions.explanation: In rows the left hand number equals the numerical value of the centre letter plus 1, the right hand number equals the reverse alphabetical value of the letter plus 1.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the empty circle?
questions.explanation: In each row, starting on the left, multiply the number by 3 and subtract 2 to give the next number on the right.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter replaces the blank and completes the puzzle?
questions.explanation: In each row, add the numerical values of the left and right hand letters to give the reverse alphabetical values of the central letter.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number comes next?
questions.explanation: Moving downwards, double each number and subtract 1.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter goes in the empty box?
questions.explanation: Letters increase in value down each column by 4 in the first column, 5 in the middle and 6 in the right hand column.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number continues this sequence?
questions.explanation: Moving downwards, add 1 to each number and double it to get the next number.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter goes in the empty circle?
questions.explanation: Starting at the top and working inwards in a clockwise spiral, letters increase in value by 4 each time.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What time should the blank watch be showing?
questions.explanation: As you move right the hour value decreases by 1, 2, 3, 4 each step and the minutes increase by 11, 12, 13 and 14.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: What goes in the empty circle?
questions.explanation: In each row the first and third numbers when read as a 2 digit number give the reverse alphabetical value of the centre letter.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing?
questions.explanation: In rows, the centre value equals the product of the left and right hand numbers minus the sum of the left and right numbers.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt:
Four men went to the building supplies centre to buy some tools for the workmen on the building sites they were in charge of. Chris buys 3 screwdrivers, 4 hammers and 5 saws for the men on his building site at a total cost of $9.70. Carl buys 4 screwdrivers, 5 hammers and 3 saws for his carpenters at a total cost of $9. Charlie’s $8.90 bought 5 screwdrivers, 3 hammers and 4 saws. Colin, who is in charge of a small building site has less money to spend but still needs 1 screwdriver, 1 hammer and a saw.

How much did he have to spend?
questions.explanation: The first three spend a total of $27.60 on 12 of each item, therefore each tool = $2.30.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which of the six smaller boxes finishes this sequence?
questions.explanation: Working in rows, add together the left and central diagrams to make the diagram on the right. If a black square appears in both of these columns it becomes white in the third box.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letters replace the blanks and complete the sequence?
questions.explanation: Letters in the bottom row are 1 place lower than the corresponding letters in the top row, letters in the third row are 2 places lower than the second row.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the empty box?
questions.explanation: The sum of the numbers in the top and bottom rows is put in the corresponding position in the second row, the difference between the top and bottom rows is put in the third row.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter is missing?
questions.explanation: Starting top left and moving clockwise in a spiral, letters move forward by 2 places, then 3, then 4 etc.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing from the middle of the circle?
questions.explanation: The numbers at the centre equal the numerical value of the letter in the opposite segment, if this value exceeds 9 the digits are added together to give a single digit answer.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number replaces the question mark?
questions.explanation: Moving in a clockwise spiral, numbers are double the square of the first 9 numbers.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number comes next?
questions.explanation: Starting with the top 3 digit number, square the central digit and add this to the original number to give the next number.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Draw the contents of the empty circle.
questions.correctAnswer: The circle pictured in the official solution.
questions.explanation: Working from left to right and using the left hand circle as a source, the middle circle shows the original and its reflection about a vertical axis, the right hand circle shows the original and its reflection about the horizontal axis.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number goes in the empty circle and completes the puzzle?
questions.explanation: The sum of the numbers in the lines of three going upwards equal the sum of the numbers in the lines of three going downwards.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which numbers complete the last two grids?
questions.explanation: The difference between the first and third columns as a 4 digit number going down is written in the central column going down.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number is missing?
questions.explanation: The sum of the odd numbers in each column equals the sum of the even numbers.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which domino completes the pattern?
questions.explanation: 30 dots in each column.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which of the three letters at the bottom fit into the top grid?
questions.explanation: Take the numerical value of each letter and multiply by the opposite to get the answer in the middle.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter replaces the blank and completes the sequence?
questions.explanation: Starting top left and moving diagonally upwards from left to right letters are repeated.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which number logically fits into the empty square?
questions.explanation: Cube the numbers in each column of the top grid and add the answers together. Write this answer going down the columns of the bottom grid.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which letter replaces the blank and completes the sequence?
questions.explanation: Cube the numerical values of the letters in the top grid and add the answers together. Write this answer in reverse order in the columns in the bottom box.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Which shape is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: The others are symmetrical.

questions.sourceOrganization: IQ Puzzles — Joe Cameron / Arcturus Publishing
questions.prompt: Complete the last row of the puzzle.
questions.explanation: There are two chains of letters in use. The first goes diagonally upwards from left to right starting in the top left corner and appears on alternate lines. This chain contains every letter of the alphabet except vowels. The second chain starts bottom right and goes diagonally downwards from right to left and contains every letter of the alphabet.
